title: Rhythms of interaction – the timescales of social coordination and why they matter
title_zh: 互动节律——社会协调的时间尺度及其意义
abstract: Social interaction involves coordination between individuals across multiple domains, including neural activity, behaviour and physiology. An increasing number of studies shows that interpersonal coordination and synchrony can be detected in each of these modalities, but the functional significance of these different types of coordination remains unclear. This paper examines the challenge of understanding coordination in terms of the timescales of interaction. We provide a novel mapping of interaction types and measurement methods across timescales spanning from milliseconds to minutes. We review candidate mechanisms of synchrony and coordination in both neural systems and behaviour, and consider how these measures relate to real world outcomes such as learning and development. Overall, we provide an integrative approach that, by taking timescales into account, aims to offer a better understanding of the origins and interpretation of interpersonal coordination.
abstract_zh: 社会互动涉及个体在多个层面之间的协调，包括神经活动、行为与生理。越来越多的研究显示，人与人之间的协调与同步可在这些模态中观察到，但不同类型协调的功能意义仍不明确。本文讨论了从互动时间尺度来理解协调的挑战。我们提供了一个跨越毫秒到分钟的时间尺度图谱，用于映射不同互动类型及其测量方法。我们回顾了神经系统与行为中同步与协调的候选机制，并讨论这些指标与现实世界结果（如学习与发展）之间的关系。总体而言，我们提出一种综合方法：通过纳入时间尺度来更好地理解人际协调的来源与解释。
